correctness.rationale: For positive mass, stiffness, friction, thermal energy and driving force in the strictly underdamped regime, independent exact Green-function and covariance calculations yield the Gaussian work law under two finite trap-center jumps. The log-concave first-lobe impulse-response lemma proves strict increase of the standardized response to the first half period; the global first-lobe response maximum and strictly accumulated noise variance exclude all later times. Algebraic high-Q expansions give the universal \(\pi^2/8\) variance ratio and the sharp Mills-tail constant. The included script completed 421 independent symbolic and numeric checks; none are substituted for continuum proofs.

originality.rationale: The known unrestricted mean-optimal protocol and its work variance (Yao--Bao--Hou 2026), earlier overdamped active protocols (Schuettler et al. 2025), and classical inertial optimal control (Gomez-Marin et al. 2008) do not state the exact two-jump class global pulse-duration and Gaussian sign-success theorem. Ordinary damped step-response, OU covariance and the ideal comparison values are prior ingredients, not claimed as discoveries. Claim-level published-record searches returned work on oscillators, harmonic numerical samplers, and work optimization in different classes rather than the stated physical two-jump Gaussian-work theorem.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 primary study explicitly leaves practical actuator constraints open. A held single-displacement trap protocol eliminates ideal Dirac impulse controls, and its exact first-half-period objective coincidence and time optimality reduce a motivated extraction/reliability design choice to one spectral parameter. The high-Q mean saturation, universal \(\pi^2/8\) variance penalty relative to the unrestricted mean-optimal protocol, and sharply exponentially rare failures are quantitative performance results, not arbitrary sample computations. Two finite instantaneous position jumps still have infinite bandwidth, which is disclosed.
